prompt: I prepare questions for my mother's doctor but forget most of them once we're in the appointment. How can I make sure the important concerns get discussed?
My father has been a little less steady and more tired this week. It's not dramatic, but it's different from usual. How should I organize these observations before contacting his healthcare team?
My mother was discharged with several instructions, and I'm not sure I understood what we're supposed to do at home or when to follow up. How can I clarify this without guessing?
I raised a concern at my father's appointment, but we ran out of time and it wasn't addressed. I don't want to sound confrontational. How can I request a follow-up discussion?

There are several medications in my mother's routine, and I have questions about timing and possible side effects. I don't want to make changes myself. What's the best way to prepare these questions for a pharmacist or clinician?
A new doctor will see my father, and I can't remember all the relevant details when asked. Can you help me create a concise summary of his recent changes, concerns, and current support needs?
At appointments I have too many concerns and end up talking about everything at once. Help me prioritize what to raise first and what can be saved for another discussion.

My mother doesn't want me speaking for her at medical appointments, but she sometimes forgets the questions she wanted to ask. How can I support her while respecting that she wants to lead the conversation?
My father has trouble hearing and misses parts of what the clinician says. He feels embarrassed when I ask people to repeat things. How can I request communication accommodations respectfully?
Two healthcare professionals gave us instructions that seem to conflict. I'm worried about choosing the wrong one. How should I clarify this safely?
We were told a test result would be discussed, but nobody has contacted us and I don't know whether we're supposed to call. How can I follow up clearly?
The clinician asked us to track some symptoms, but I don't want to create a complicated spreadsheet. What is the simplest useful way to record what happens?
I have only a few minutes to speak to my mother's clinic and need to explain why I'm concerned. Help me organize a short, clear message that gets the main point across.
The doctor recommended another appointment or assessment, but I didn't fully understand why or how soon it should happen. What questions should I ask to clarify the recommendation?
My father gets anxious before medical appointments and sometimes refuses to go. How can I prepare him in a calm, respectful way without overwhelming him with details?
I'm concerned my mother may not be safe doing a task she has always done independently. I don't want to unnecessarily restrict her. How can I describe the concern and ask for guidance?
We have appointment letters, medication lists, notes, and test paperwork scattered around. I need a simple way to organize what to bring without spending hours sorting everything.
After my father's appointment, my siblings want an update, but I don't want to misinterpret the clinician or start another argument. How can I share the key information clearly?
We have a follow-up appointment scheduled in a few weeks, but my mother's symptoms have changed since the last visit. How can I decide whether to contact the clinic sooner rather than wait?

We just finished a medical appointment and I have a few recommendations, referrals, and things to monitor. I'm overwhelmed. Can you help me turn the information into a short action list with priorities?
